# k0rdent_networks (Data Source)

Every network in a project, including the ones a cluster created for itself.

A cluster-provisioned network carries a `cluster_id` and cannot be written through the tenant API. This is the only way a configuration can see one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Includes networks a cluster made for itself. Those have a `cluster_id` and
# can't be managed.
data "k0rdent_networks" "all" {
  # Read after the cluster exists, so its networks are listed.
  depends_on = [k0rdent_kubernetes_cluster.training]
}

output "cluster_networks" {
  value = [for n in data.k0rdent_networks.all.networks : n.id if n.cluster_id != null]
}

# Only the ones a k0rdent_network could manage.
data "k0rdent_networks" "mine" {
  only_tenant_owned = true
}

# The production network, found by tags instead of a hardcoded id. The
# postcondition fails the plan unless exactly one matches.
data "k0rdent_networks" "prod" {
  tags               = { env = "prod", team = "ml" }
  display_name_regex = "^prod-"
  state              = "active"

  lifecycle {
    postcondition {
      condition     = length(self.ids) == 1
      error_message = "Expected exactly one active network tagged env=prod, team=ml."
    }
  }
}

output "prod_network" {
  value = one(data.k0rdent_networks.prod.ids)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `display_name_regex` (String) Return only the networks whose `display_name` matches this regular expression, in the RE2 syntax Terraform's own `regex` function takes. The match isn't anchored, so `prod` finds `preprod-a`: write `^prod-` for a prefix. One with no `display_name` never matches. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Must be a regular expression in RE2 syntax.
- `only_tenant_owned` (Boolean) Return only the networks with no `cluster_id`, which are the ones a `k0rdent_network` can manage. Filtered in the provider: the list operation takes no filter.
- `project` (String) Project to read. Defaults to the provider's `project`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `state` (String) Return only the networks whose `state` is this value. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["creating" "active" "updating" "deleting" "failed"].
- `tags` (Map of String) Return only the networks carrying every one of these tags with exactly this value. Tags beyond these don't matter. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Every tag value must be set: a null value matches nothing.

### Read-Only

- `ids` (List of String) Just the ids, for `for_each` and `contains`. Sorted by `id`, at the same positions as `networks`.
- `networks` (Attributes List) The networks, sorted by `id`, which is the network's name. That order is stable when the platform reorders them but not when one is added, so reach an element with `for_each` rather than `networks[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--networks))

<a id="nestedatt--networks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `networks`

Read-Only:

- `cluster_id` (String) UID of the cluster that provisioned it. Null on a network a tenant created, set on one the cluster lifecycle owns.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name, for display only.
- `id` (String) The network's name.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this object.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state as last read from the platform.
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined labels, as key-value pairs. Null when the object has none.
- `type` (String) `evpn`, `infiniband` or `nvlink`.
- `vpc` (String) The fabric VPC this network attaches to, on a cluster-provisioned network.
